# local 0004: mcs51: compiler crash for functions with a function attribute that return a struct and have a non-struct first parameter

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. ds390, whose reg_parm also tests the return type, was not built.
- Patch: [local-0004.patch](../../patches/local-0004.patch), commit [`5bb1bd405`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/5bb1bd405789954aee6964448e80a8a96c6e5bb4). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176, `sdcc -mmcs51 -c r1.c` ends with `Caught signal 11: SIGSEGV` for this file.

```c
struct s { unsigned char a; int b; unsigned char c; };
struct s r1 (unsigned char x) __reentrant { struct s r; r.a = x; r.b = 1; r.c = 2; return r; }
```

gdb shows the fault in `genMove_o` in `src/mcs51/gen.c`, which `genReceive` calls through
`genMove` with a null pointer as the source. The compiler also crashes with `--stack-auto`, with
`--model-large`, and with `__critical` or `__using (0)` in the place of `__reentrant`. Without a
function attribute the file compiles.

On r17192 with the earlier patches of this report, the cause has three more effects. For calls of
`r1` that are compiled from its declaration, the code does not pass the argument. A `__reentrant`
function with a `long` parameter that returns a union compiles, and it reads the parameter from
registers that callers do not load. For a call through a pointer to the function type of `r1`,
the compiler stops at an assertion in `genPcall`.

## Cause

`_mcs51_regparm` in `src/mcs51/main.c` returns 0 for every parameter of functions that return a
struct or union, and `aopArg` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` does too. The registers stay free for the
hidden pointer to the result. `processFunc` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` sets `SPEC_REGPARM` and
`SPEC_ARGREG` for parameters for which the port's `reg_parm` returns nonzero, and it does not
clear them when a later call returns 0. `addDecl` calls `processFunc` each time it adds a part to
a type that contains a function declarator. For a declarator with function attributes, the action
of `declarator2_function_attributes` in `src/SDCC.y` makes the first of these calls before the
return type is in the type, and `_mcs51_regparm` returns 1 for `x`. It returns 0 in the two later
calls, as observed in gdb, and the mark of the first call stays. The front end then generates
`RECEIVE` and `SEND` for parameters for which `aopArg` returns 0.

## Fix

When `reg_parm` returns 0, `processFunc` clears both flags in the type of the parameter and in
the type of its symbol. All ports use `processFunc`. The change has an effect only for parameters
that an earlier call marked.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/struct-return-funcattr.c` has 20 assertions for functions with
`__reentrant` and `__using (0)`, with two parameters, and with a union return and a `long`
parameter. Three of its calls are compiled from declarations, one of them through a function
pointer. On r17192 the test does not compile for mcs51 with the small, medium, large, and huge
models and with `--stack-auto` for the small and large models. With the patch, which was tested
together with the earlier patches of this report, it passes on these six variants and on host.
On stm8 and ucz80 it passes with and without the patch.

With the series of this report up to this patch applied to r17192, the regression suite has 0
failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The diagnostics suite has 0 failures
for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. This patch and the patches for local
0002 and local 0006 were compared together with the series without them. For stm8 and ucz80 the
assembly of the regression tests is identical. For the mcs51 variants it differs in 11 to 17
files per variant, and each difference is a jump that stays long because of the patch for local
0006.

`_ds390_regparm` in `src/ds390/main.c` tests the return type too, and since r17076 it clears the
two flags in the type of the parameter itself. ds390 was not built.

## Related

- `__critical` functions that return a struct return a wrong value on mcs51 and z80, with and
  without parameters. Compiled by r17192, a test of `struct s crit (void) __critical` fails 3 of
  6 assertions on mcs51-large and on ucz80. With the patch, the file above with `__critical`
  compiles and returns a wrong value, and the test of the patch does not have such a function. By
  the source, `genRet` of mcs51 computes the stack offset of the result pointer without the byte
  that the entry code of `__critical` functions pushes. This was not confirmed in a debugger.
- Bug #3847 concerns functions that return the struct value of a call. Its patch does not change
  this defect.
